body.description: National figures from Common App's own End-of-Season reports (August each year): first-year applicants, applications, applications per applicant, member institutions, and year-over-year growth for fee-waiver-eligible and first-generation applicants, typed from the key-findings text with a page and a verbatim quote. These are Common App's counts of its members' applicants, not federal data. State-level figures are appendix tables printed as images in the PDF and are left out (specs/data-expansion/common-app.md).

rows.quote: 1,527,328 distinct first-year applicants applied to 1,146 member institutions, an increase of 2% from 1,495,475 applicants in 2024–25.
First-year applications increased from 10,157,068 in 2024–25 to 10,786,782 in 2025–26, an increase of 6%, as illustrated in Figure 5.
Figure 6 illustrates that applications per applicant increased 4% from 6.79 in 2024–25 to 7.06 in 2025–26.
Figure 1 charts growth in the number of member institutions receiving applications from 1,097 in 2024–25 to 1,146 in 2025–26, an increase of 4%.
1,527,328 distinct first-year applicants applied to 1,146 member institutions, an increase of 2% from 1,495,475 applicants in 2024–25.
Applicants reporting eligibility for the Common App fee waiver grew at over five times the rate of other applicants (6% versus less than 1%) between the 2024–25 and 2025–26 seasons.
Applicants identifying as first-generation grew at a rate of 6%, while continuing-generation applicants declined by less than 1% from 2024–25 to 2025–26.
In 2025-26, 5% of members require a test score to submit an application.
1,498,199 distinct first-year applicants applied to 1,097 member institutions, an increase of 5% from 1,423,466 applicants in 2023–24.
First-year applications increased from 9,447,544 in 2023–24 to 10,193,579 in 2024–25, an increase of 8%, as illustrated in Figure 5.
Figure 6 illustrates that applications per applicant increased 2% from 6.64 in 2023–24 to 6.80 in 2024–25.
Figure 1 charts growth in the number of member institutions receiving applications from 1,068 in 2023–24 to 1,097 in 2024–25, an increase of 3%.
1,498,199 distinct first-year applicants applied to 1,097 member institutions, an increase of 5% from 1,423,466 applicants in 2023–24.
Applicants reporting eligibility for the Common App fee waiver grew at over three times the rate of other applicants (10% versus 3%) between the 2023–24 and 2024–25 seasons.
Applicants identifying as first-generation grew at a substantial rate of 14%, while continuing-gen applicants grew 1% from 2023–24 to 2024–25.
This season, 5% of members require a test score to submit an application.
